text: Behind the house, which they had thought empty, stood about twenty German soldiers, and a huge, hairy officer sat on a chair, smoking a large pipe. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, gentlemen, did you have good fishing, he asked in excellent French, as a soldier laid the net of fish at his feet. <break time="0.8s" /> You are spies to me, and spies are shot, he said, but give me your password, and you may go free. <break time="0.8s" /> Pale and side by side, their hands trembling a little, the two friends said nothing, even when the officer took each of them aside in turn. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then Morissots eyes fell on the net of gudgeons in the grass, where the little fish were still shining and moving in the sun. <break time="0.8s" /> A weakness came over him, and despite all his efforts his eyes filled with tears, so he said softly, Goodbye, Monsieur Sauvage. <break time="0.8s" /> Goodbye, Monsieur Morissot, answered Sauvage, and they shook hands, trembling from head to foot, and then, at the officers command, twelve rifles fired as one. <break time="0.8s" /> The two friends fell to the ground together, and the soldiers carried them to the river, whose waters soon became calm again. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the officer picked up the net, smiled, and called to his cook, Fry these little creatures at once, while they are still alive.
